applicability: Applies to inputs matching the schema: 1 to 8 integer operands each in [-10,20], and exactly len(operands)-1 operators drawn from '+','-','*'. Returns the number of distinct values over all full parenthesizations preserving operand and operator order. Rejects malformed inputs, wrong key sets, booleans, non-integers, out-of-range operands, wrong operator count, and unknown operators via ValueError. Uses Python arbitrary-precision integers, so intermediate products are exact. Not applicable to expressions with other operators, reordering, or non-integer operands.
description: Interval dynamic programming over contiguous operand subranges. For each subrange [i,j], dp[i][j] is the set of all distinct values obtainable by fully parenthesizing operands i..j with operators i..j-1. Base case single operand. For longer ranges, split at every k and combine every left value with every right value using operator[k], inserting into a set to deduplicate. The answer is the cardinality of dp[0][n-1]. This exactly enumerates all full binary parenthesizations preserving order. Uncertainty: assumes the intended interpretation is all full parenthesizations (Catalan many), which matches the problem wording; if a restricted parenthesization class were intended the count could differ, but the stated problems indicate full parenthesization.
